speaker: Doctor
text: The Eosinophil Count and Creatine Kinase levels are normal, and the MRI of the legs shows no signs of deep vein thrombosis or myositis. Since your blood work is fully normal and you've been camping recently, have you noticed any swollen or painful lymph nodes, or have you experienced any unexplained weight loss or night sweats?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness and fatigue. I also have Mild diplopia.

speaker: Doctor
text:
You mentioned having mild diplopia (double vision) alongside your weakness and fatigue. Is this diplopia constant or does it fluctuate, and does it improve when you close one eye? Also, have you noticed any difficulty swallowing or breathing?

REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibody; REQUEST TEST: Anti-Jo1_Antibody

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibody: Positive; Anti-Jo1_Antibody: Not Detected

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis

The positive Acetylcholine Receptor Antibody test, combined with your symptoms of fluctuating weakness, fatigue, and mild diplopia, confirms a diagnosis of Myasthenia Gravis. The negative Anti-Jo1 antibody rules out Myositis, and the normal blood work excludes systemic infections or thyroid issues.
